brief.hook: Before you even ask me what stocks to buy, I want to know these questions first.
keep: The closer you are to needing that dollar, the more conservative you should be: bank accounts for the next three years, your own risk for four to 10 years, and at 10 years expect a down year once or twice. With 10+ years you can play your game, depending on what you're investing in.

editorPlan.title: Before you invest $1, answer these
editorPlan.rationale: The video argues that stock picks are the wrong first question: emergency savings and when you need the money come first. The hook leads with the exact question beginners ask and refuses to answer it, which creates tension and sets up the closing line. The payoff is the time-bucket rule. Money you need soon goes in bank accounts, a 10-year goal should expect down years, and the closer you get to needing it, the safer it goes; then it loops back to 'answer these first' and the punchline.

storyline.headline: STOCK PICKS? NOT YET.
storyline.viewerNeeds: Big text 'Which stock should I buy?' gets crossed out and replaced with 'Answer these first'.

storyline.headline: Q2: WHEN DO YOU NEED IT?
Q2: WHEN DO YOU NEED IT?
TIME BUCKETS
storyline.viewerNeeds: Three empty buckets labeled 0–3 yrs, 3–10 yrs, 10+ yrs build in under the headline.

storyline.headline: SOON = BANK ACCOUNT
storyline.viewerNeeds: The 0–3 yrs bucket fills with 'bank account' on the words 'bank accounts'; the rest stay grey on 'your own risk'.

storyline.headline: 10 YEARS = 1–2 DOWN YEARS
storyline.viewerNeeds: A 10-year strip of boxes; one or two turn red on 'once or twice'.

storyline.headline: CLOSER = SAFER
storyline.viewerNeeds: Gradient bar, risky on the far end sliding to conservative as the goal gets closer.

editorPlan.coldViewer: Hook is clear and relatable in about 4 s. Emergency fund is quick and the 'kid' line adds personality. The highest drop risk is 9–10 (abstract 'time buckets'); the bucket graphic has to carry it, and the 3–4 year line lands the stake fast. The 1-in-4 stat is unverified per the brief. It is roughly in line with the historical share of negative calendar years for US stocks, but it should get a quick fact-check before posting. Line 29 repeats 'three years' after 11–12, but it adds the concrete 'bank accounts' answer and the disclaimer, so it reads as the conclusion. Junctions hold: 'that's why' points at the 1-in-4 stat, and 'those questions' points back to the hook. The quotable line is 'Stop asking me for advice.' Runs about 68–72 s from roughly 195 words at his pace. Honest score is a 6.5: useful and in voice, but no real reversal.
